messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: hosted-api requests queue length > 20k across eu-west-1 GPU pools. Severity: P1. Impact: p95 request latency > 30s, some 504s. @Anna (oncall) paged.
Anna (oncall): acked — looking now. any immediate customer-facing impact? if so, ping support.
Jen (support): seeing multiple customer reports about timeouts and UI errors since 09:12 UTC. Ticket counts up. Will prepare customer-facing status message if we need an incident status page — hold for confirmed mitigation.
Priya (sre): I'm seeing autoscaler logs showing repeated "scale-up throttled" errors from cloud provider. Autoscaler attempted 5 scale ops in last 7m, hit quota and 429 from provider. GPU pool utilization at 98%.
Miguel (eng-runtime): runtime metrics: KV cache hits low (4%), seq-lens normal. Spike seems request count heavy from a small set of API keys — per-key qps strongly skewed. Likely a traffic burst from a few tenants.
Sara (eng-runtime): Confirmed. Router traces show 3 API keys account for ~65% of queued requests. We can flip routing rules to send those keys to a degraded smaller model or to Dedicated fallback if available.
Anna (oncall): options: 1) increase autoscaler max nodes (manual), 2) redirect heavy customers to smaller model, 3) apply temporary global throttle for non-critical endpoints, 4) open cloud support ticket for quota. Which is fastest?
Priya (sre): Fastest: manual bump of autoscaler max_nodes + short-lived rate-limit for offending keys. I'm going to raise max_nodes to 120 and restart scaler. If provider still 429s we need fallback routing.
Miguel (eng-runtime): I'll prepare the routing change. Proposed policy: route keys in list X -> model-redwood-small-quantized and mark low-priority generation endpoints with 503-forced when queue > 10k.
Tom (product-ops): Agree on routing for immediate relief. We'll need to record the customer impact and follow up with communications. Jen, once mitigation is stable can you draft an update for status.redwood.ai?
Jen (support): on it. Drafting message: "We're mitigating a service delay impacting text generation. Customers may see elevated latencies or temporary 503s for non-critical requests. More updates shortly." Will post after you confirm.
Priya (sre): Running commands now:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/autoscaler MAX_NODES=120
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/autoscaler
```
Priya (sre): Autoscaler restarted, logs show initial scale attempts. Cloud provider still returning 429 for create-instance calls but we have running nodes coming online from spare capacity (12 nodes). Queue dropped from 23k -> 16k in ~3m.
Anna (oncall): good progress. Miguel, status on routing flip?
Miguel (eng-runtime): Applying routing override for keys. Patch:
```
route: if api_key in ["k_ABC123","k_DEF456","k_GHI789"] -> model: redwood-small-quant
limit: max_concurrent_per_key: 20
```
Miguel (eng-runtime): Patch applied. Those keys now go to the smaller model. Observed immediate drop in queue for their shards.
Sara (eng-runtime): Also enabled legacy prefix caching for common prompts: cache hit rate bumped to 28% — helps a lot for repeated patterns.
Anna (oncall): queue now 8.3k, p95 down to 3.1s, p99 still ~12s. Any residual errors?
Jen (support): Support tickets stabilizing; some customers acknowledge degraded fidelity acceptable for now. I'll notify account teams for the top-3 affected customers.
Tom (product-ops): Good. Let's keep throttles in place until cloud quota is resolved and autoscaler backfilled. Post-incident action: review per-key qps protections.
Priya (sre): Opening cloud support ticket (INC-1987) for quota bump. Also scheduling postmortem to evaluate autoscaler backoff behavior. Will collect logs.
Anna (oncall): I'm going to hand off to Priya for long-running follow-up. Priya — you're oncall owner for the rest of the incident. I'll update the pager duty handoff.
Priya (sre): Ack. I'll monitor until p99 < 5s and queue < 1k. Next steps: validate autoscaler recovered, keep routing overrides queued for rollback. ETA 45m.
incident-bot: Incident channel pinned. Incident created: hosted-api-gpu-starvation-1923456789
Jen (support): Posting status update now and linking this thread. :thumbsup: 
Miguel (eng-runtime): Quick note — logs for the offending API keys attached to the incident ticket. We'll prepare per-customer follow-up guidance (rate limits, upgrade path to Dedicated).
Anna (oncall): thanks team. Handing off — Priya will publish timeline + RCA once we have root cause.
